hints: Clear the trigonometric denominators, then replace $\sin^2\theta$ by $1-\cos^2\theta$.
Collect the terms as a quadratic in $\cos^2\theta$.
walkthrough:
Express $\cot\theta$, $\tan\theta$, and $\sin 2\theta$ in terms of $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$ using definition and double angle identities:
$$\cot\theta = \dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}, \quad \tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}, \quad \sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta$$

Substitute these into the given equation $\cot\theta - 2\tan\theta = \sin 2\theta$:
$$\dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta} - 2\left(\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\right) = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta$$

Clear fractions by multiplying through by the common denominator $\sin\theta\cos\theta$:
$$\cos\theta(\cos\theta) - 2\sin\theta(\sin\theta) = (2\sin\theta\cos\theta)(\sin\theta\cos\theta)$$
$$\cos^2\theta - 2\sin^2\theta = 2\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta$$

Use the Pythagorean identity $\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta$ to write all terms entirely in terms of $\cos\theta$:
$$\cos^2\theta - 2(1 - \cos^2\theta) = 2(1 - \cos^2\theta)\cos^2\theta$$

Rearrange all terms to the left-hand side to form a 3-term polynomial in $\cos^2\theta$:
$$2\cos^4\theta + (3\cos^2\theta - 2\cos^2\theta) - 2 = 0$$
$$2\cos^4\theta + \cos^2\theta - 2 = 0$$

Identify the required constants:
$$a = 2, \quad b = 1, \quad c = -2$$

hints: Treat the equation from part (i) as a quadratic in $u=\cos^2\theta$.
Reject any value of $u$ outside $0\le u\le1$, then choose the negative value of $\cos\theta$ because $90^\circ<\theta<180^\circ$.
Apply inverse cosine and give the single angle in the stated interval.
walkthrough:
Treat the equation $2\cos^4\theta + \cos^2\theta - 2 = 0$ as a quadratic in $u = \cos^2\theta$:
$$2u^2 + u - 2 = 0$$

Apply the quadratic formula with $A = 2, B = 1, C = -2$:
$$u = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1^2 - 4(2)(-2)}}{2(2)} = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1 + 16}}{4} = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{17}}{4}$$

Since $u = \cos^2\theta \ge 0$ for all real $\theta$, discard $u_2 < 0$. Thus:
$$\cos^2\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{17} - 1}{4} \approx 0.780776$$

Determine the sign of $\cos\theta$ for the specified second quadrant interval $90^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$:
In the second quadrant, cosine is negative, so choose the negative square root:
$$\cos\theta = -\sqrt{\dfrac{\sqrt{17} - 1}{4}} \approx -\sqrt{0.780776} \approx -0.883615$$

State the unique solution rounded to 1 decimal place:
$$\theta = 152.1^\circ$$
